resources.string: Open Market OS
Connect to your computer

This app shows Open Market OS running on your own computer, over your home network. On the computer, open Open Market OS → Settings → Devices, switch on “Allow devices on my network”, then press “Create one-time code”.
Scan pairing code
Or type the address and code shown on the computer:
One-time code
Connect
Point the camera at the square code on your computer’s Settings → Devices page
That is not an Open Market OS pairing code.
Type the address shown on the computer, like 192.168.1.20:8766.
Type the one-time code shown on the computer (letters and digits).
Checking the computer’s certificate…
Certificate check
This phone sees certificate check %1$s.\n\nThe computer shows its certificate check on Settings → Devices. Is it the same?
Same, connect
Different
Not connected: another device may be posing as your computer. Check that both are on your own network, then try again.
Cannot reach %1$s. Is the phone on the same Wi-Fi as the computer, and is network access switched on there?
Cannot reach the computer. Is the phone on the same Wi-Fi, and is Open Market OS running with network access switched on?
This code has no certificate. Update Open Market OS on the computer, or type the address and code instead.
Connecting…
The computer refused: %1$s. Create a new code on the computer (codes work once, for 5 minutes).
Pairing failed: %1$s

The computer presented a different certificate than the one this phone paired with. If you reinstalled Open Market OS or reset its data, pair again. Otherwise, another device may be posing as your computer.
Cannot reach your computer. It may be off or asleep, on another network, or Open Market OS may be closed.
Try again
Pair again
Forget this computer on this phone? You can pair again with a new code. (To sign this phone out on the computer too, revoke it in Settings → Devices.)
